prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1125; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound through the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when a vehicle traveling westbound entered the intersection and struck the driver's side of Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the struck vehicle, and a Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat. Driver 2 is the claimant in this report and reported neck and back strain at the scene, a complaint consistent with the forces typical of a broadside collision of this type. Responding officers observed damage to the driver's side door and quarter panel that matches the described direction of impact. Scene photographs confirm the general positions of the vehicles and the damage pattern, although they do not capture every detail of the approach. No independent witnesses were located, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known to officers or to the owner. Both the responding officers and the persons on scene confirmed that Driver 2 was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Driver 2 is identified as a household member of the policyholder, residing at the same address.
